title.en: Blender view transform to three.js tone mapping table

summary: Pair one Blender view transform with one three.js tone-mapping constant before comparing renders, and fix output color space, colour management and exposure as part of the same declaration.
objective: Every Blender-to-three.js comparison names one mapped pair of view transform and tone-mapping constant, so an appearance difference can be attributed to lighting or materials rather than to the output transform.
intent_signals: which three.js tone mapping matches AgX
Blender render looks different in the web viewer
what is the equivalent of Filmic in three.js
should I use ACESFilmic or AgX tone mapping
set output color space and tone mapping
example_prompts: Match my Blender AgX look in a three.js viewer before I start adjusting materials.
Tell me which three.js tone mapping constant corresponds to the Khronos PBR Neutral view.
not_for: Guaranteeing pixel identity between two renderers.
Colour science derivation or display calibration.
Choosing an artistic grade; this record fixes the transform so the grade can be judged.

principles: A view transform is an output decision applied at the end of the pipeline. Comparing two images rendered under different transforms says nothing about the materials underneath them.

The mapping is a small closed table, not a family of near-equivalents. Three of Blender's views have a same-named counterpart in the renderer's tone-mapping enumeration; the rest do not, and an unmapped view must be re-viewed rather than approximated.
Tone mapping and output color space are two separate settings and must both be declared. A dark or washed image is as often a colour-space mistake as a tone-mapping one.
Exposure is the only variable left once the pair is fixed. Compare at the documented default of 1 first; any other value is a deliberate grade that belongs in the report.
implementation: Map the transform, one row at a time: Blender `Standard` -> `NoToneMapping` (the renderer's documented default); Blender `AgX` -> `AgXToneMapping`; Blender `Khronos PBR Neutral` -> `NeutralToneMapping`.

Blender `Filmic` has no counterpart. The documented `toneMapping` enumeration is `NoToneMapping | LinearToneMapping | ReinhardToneMapping | CineonToneMapping | ACESFilmicToneMapping | CustomToneMapping | AgXToneMapping | NeutralToneMapping` and contains no Filmic constant; `ACESFilmicToneMapping` is a separately named transform and neither page states that the two curves agree. The Blender manual marks `Filmic` deprecated and superseded by `AgX`, so re-view a Filmic reference under `AgX` before comparing rather than substituting `ACESFilmicToneMapping`.

Declare the whole output decision once at renderer construction:
```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer( { antialias: true } );
THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = true;              // documented default
renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;  // documented default
renderer.toneMapping = THREE.AgXToneMapping;       // pairs with Blender's AgX view
renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0;                // documented default; declare it anyway
```

`renderer.outputColorSpace` accepts `SRGBColorSpace` or `LinearSRGBColorSpace` and is documented to default to `SRGBColorSpace`. Keep `SRGBColorSpace` for a display target; treat `LinearSRGBColorSpace` as a hand-off to an external grading step, never as a remedy for an image that looks too dark.

`THREE.ColorManagement.enabled` is documented as enabled by default and is what makes hexadecimal and CSS colour setters convert sRGB input into the Linear-sRGB working space. Record its value beside the comparison; do not toggle it to chase a match, because it changes every authored colour literal at once.

Annotate colour textures loaded outside the glTF path with `texture.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace` and leave data maps unannotated, so the table above is comparing transforms rather than a decoding mistake.

Record the pair in the comparison report as `blender_view` and `three_tone_mapping` columns plus `outputColorSpace` and `toneMappingExposure`. A column whose Blender view is unmapped is flagged, not silently paired with the nearest-looking constant.
observable_checks: Switching only `renderer.toneMapping` between `NoToneMapping` and `AgXToneMapping` changes the rendered image while glTF material factors and texture bytes stay identical.

A scene rendered with `toneMapping = NoToneMapping` and `outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace` is closer to a Blender `Standard` view than to any other row; if it is not, the difference lives in lighting or materials.
Setting `THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = false` visibly changes hexadecimal-authored colours, which identifies which colours pass through the conversion.
The comparison report names one Blender view and one tone-mapping constant per column; a column reading `Filmic` is reported as unmapped rather than compared.

known_limits: The mapping is by shared name and documented intent. Neither source states that a Blender view and a same-named renderer constant implement an identical curve, so the pairing is a comparison protocol, not an equivalence proof.
Blender's view list and the renderer's tone-mapping enumeration both change between releases; the Blender page read here was the latest channel and the renderer page is unversioned.
The renderer page enumerates constants but prints no curve definitions, so no statement is made here about how any two transforms differ numerically.
Authored reusable guidance: no render, screenshot or numeric image comparison was produced for this record.
creative_affordances: Any row may be chosen as the final look; the requirement is that the chosen pair is named, not that it is the most neutral one.
Exposure may be pushed away from 1 as a deliberate grade once the pair has been compared at 1.

claims.statement: The Blender manual's Views list describes Standard as doing no extra conversion besides the conversion for the display, Khronos PBR Neutral as a tone mapping transform designed specifically for PBR color accuracy, AgX as a tone mapping transform that improves on Filmic and offers 16.5 stops of dynamic range, and Filmic as deprecated and superseded by AgX.
claims.scope: The documented view descriptions on the accessed page of the latest manual channel. The page prints no transfer curves, so no numerical relationship between views is asserted.

source_refs.locator: Views: "Standard: Does no extra conversion besides the conversion for the display"; "Khronos PBR Neutral: A tone mapping transform designed specifically for PBR color accuracy"; "AgX: A tone mapping transform that improves on Filmic, giving more photorealistic results. AgX offers 16.5 stops of dynamic range"; "Filmic: ... Filmic is deprecated and is superseded by AgX which improves handling of saturated colors"

claims.statement: The renderer documents toneMapping as one of NoToneMapping, LinearToneMapping, ReinhardToneMapping, CineonToneMapping, ACESFilmicToneMapping, CustomToneMapping, AgXToneMapping or NeutralToneMapping with a default of NoToneMapping, toneMappingExposure as the exposure level of tone mapping with a default of 1, and outputColorSpace as SRGBColorSpace or LinearSRGBColorSpace with a default of SRGBColorSpace; the enumeration contains no constant named for Blender's Filmic view.
claims.scope: The documented property enumerations and defaults of one unversioned library page as accessed. The absence of a Filmic constant is an observation about this list, not about any release's internal shader code.

source_refs.locator: toneMapping : NoToneMapping | LinearToneMapping | ReinhardToneMapping | CineonToneMapping | ACESFilmicToneMapping | CustomToneMapping | AgXToneMapping | NeutralToneMapping, "Default is NoToneMapping"; toneMappingExposure "Exposure level of tone mapping. Default is 1"; outputColorSpace : SRGBColorSpace | LinearSRGBColorSpace, "Default is SRGBColorSpace"

claims.statement: The renderer's colour-management documentation states that certain conversions for hexadecimal and CSS sRGB colours are made automatically when the ColorManagement API is enabled through THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = true, that ColorManagement is enabled by default, and that PNG or JPEG colour textures must be annotated with texture.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace while the working space is Linear-sRGB.
claims.scope: Documented colour-management behaviour of one library as accessed. It concerns input annotation and automatic conversion, not tone mapping or display calibration.
